gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the Starlink Mini can run from a power station's 12 V car outlet through Starlink's own Mini Car Adapter (12–24 V in, 60 W out), which leaves the station's one full-power USB-C port free for the MacBook. Anker's US spec table for the SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 gives the 20V/5A, 140 W rating only to USB-C 2 and puts USB-C 1 in a 20 W total shared with USB-A, so on that station the Mini and the MacBook can't both run from USB-C.
standout_why: Pages compared: the cited Starlink help articles (both JavaScript-only; their 100 W / 20V/5A figure is confirmed by the Mini spec sheet), starsurf.com (says only '100 W USB-C PD or 12–48 V DC' and 'a 12 V DC connection or a suitable USB-C PD adapter', names no adapter or ports) and kilohour.com (says 'check the port lists 20 V/5 A' and counts car ports of 60 W or more, but says nothing about two USB-C ports sharing a power budget or about Starlink's car adapter). None of the three ChatGPT answers names the Mini Car Adapter or says which port on a named station can power the Mini and which the MacBook. ChatGPT only said: 'If you need two USB-C outputs, check the station's individual port ratings.'
decides: This confirms the C1000 Gen 2 as a 1 kWh pick but changes how it gets wired. If USB-C 1 really is capped at 20 W, the MacBook takes the 140 W USB-C 2 and the Mini goes on the 12V/10A (120 W) car outlet through the Starlink Mini Car Adapter. That avoids the AC inverter, which is the efficiency point ChatGPT raised without saying how. Our current page cell 'C1000 Gen 2: 2× 140 W' disagrees with Anker's US spec table and needs fixing. Rule for every candidate: the station needs either two USB-C ports that each offer 20V/5A at the same time, or one such port plus a 12 V car outlet rated about 60 W or more for the Mini Car Adapter.

findings.label: Starlink Mini Car Adapter: input, output and contents
findings.value: Accepts 12–24 V; USB-C output rated 60 W; kit = 12 V adapter plus 5 m (16.4 ft) Mini USB-C cable; DishyTech paid $45 at Starlink
findings.source_title: Starlink Mini 12V Car Adapter Review – DishyTech
findings.note: DishyTech says the adapter 'can be plugged into a vehicle, RV, or portable power station' and that they ran it from an EcoFlow River 2. DishyTech quotes Starlink's product page: 'the car adapter and USB-C cable can't be used with other devices.' The cable LED turns red if the source is incompatible or the adapter overheats. The $45 price is DishyTech's purchase, not today's Starlink price.
